title: Carrot and beetroot slaw on goat's cheese toast

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a plain whole food or simple staple, such as carrots, beetroot, orange, honey, bread and goat's cheese.

supermarket.reason: Raw beetroot, soft goat's cheese and pumpkin seeds are all everyday items at Tesco and similar supermarkets.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, a grater and a bowl, and the techniques are simple grating, dressing and toasting.

works.reason: Three carrots and two beetroot dressed with orange, oil, vinegar and honey make enough slaw for eight slices of toast, and 150g of goat's cheese spreads across them for four.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes to grate five roots, make the dressing and toast and spread the bread is believable, and five minutes covers toasting the seeds, so it fits a quick lunch.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, cumin included, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Stored carrots and beetroot with European oranges suit February, and carrot leads the slaw rather than garnishing it.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling lunch of wholemeal toast, cheese, seeds and plenty of raw vegetables.
